outcome: LOADED AND VERIFIED. Tier 3 is live, noindex, in no sitemap child and not disallowed. IndexNow is skipped for this tier by design. The Tier 2 redirect-chain blocker was closed before the load and no chain remains.

blockerClearedFirst.why: The Tier 2 record closed with a blocker for this stage: that load wrote risedronate-sodium-hemi-pentahydrate -> risedronate while a row from 2026-09-02 already said risedronate-sodium-hemipentahydrate -> risedronate-sodium-hemi-pentahydrate. resolvePublicMedicineRoute refuses a redirect whose target is itself an old slug, so a URL that had been answering 308 was answering 404 in production. Tier 3 writes 176 more redirects and could have made more of them, so this was closed before any Tier 3 row was written.
blockerClearedFirst.confirmedBeforeTheFix: select from medicine_slug_redirects joined to itself through drugs returned exactly one chain, and https://rnawiki.com/d/risedronate-sodium-hemipentahydrate answered 404.
blockerClearedFirst.change: scripts/corpus-20k/load/materialise.ts now reads the ledger with each row's target slug and holds a redirect to one hop in three places: a pre-flight pass walks every chain already in the ledger to its terminal drug and re-points the earlier hops, keeping each row's own recorded reason and rationale; a redirect this run would write onto a slug that is itself an old slug is re-pointed to that chain's terminal drug instead of being written as a first hop; and an existing row whose target this run turns into an old slug is re-pointed, in the same transaction, to where the new row points. A cycle is never repaired - the load refuses, because a cycle has no terminal target and choosing one would be a guess about which URL is canonical. One row per old slug per batch, because ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE cannot touch the same row twice in one statement.
blockerClearedFirst.test: tests/unit/corpus-20k/load-redirect-chains.test.ts - 7 cases over terminalSlugOf and repairLedgerChains, including the exact risedronate ledger, a ledger with no chain, a terminal slug with no legacy drugs row, and a cycle.
blockerClearedFirst.dryRunBeforeTheLoad: The Tier 3 dry run reported the one existing chain as the only repair and the same 22636 pages, 91 batches and 176 redirects as before the change, so the guard changed what the ledger holds and nothing about what the tier writes.
blockerClearedFirst.liveAfter: /d/risedronate-sodium-hemipentahydrate and /d/risedronate-sodium-hemi-pentahydrate both answer 308 to /d/risedronate, which answers 200.
blockerClearedFirst.notDeployed: The change is to a workstation loader, not to the web service. No deployment, no migration; production still holds 26 migrations.

load.whyNoneIsIndexable: The loader sets indexable only for tier <= 2 (materialise.ts: `tier <= 2 && pageType !== 'stub' && presentFieldCount >= threshold`), so R6's rule is a property of the row, not of a later filter. No Tier 3 page can become indexable by gaining fields without a tier change.

load.reRunSkipsRecordedBatches: The same command run a second time against production reported batches 91, skipped 91, pages 0 and wrote nothing; the chain pre-flight found nothing to repair.

tier3FieldCounts.reading: No Tier 3 page reaches 11 present fields, so the tier is noindex twice over: by the loader's tier rule and by the threshold itself. 752 Tier 3 pages sit at 7 fields, inside the 7-10 promotion band.

sitemapCacheWait.why: The sitemap index, each child body and the corpus facet record set are three independent 15-minute per-process caches, so a freshly loaded tier does not appear at once. Tier 2 recorded the same window.
sitemapCacheWait.tier3ChildIsNotPolled: /sitemaps/tier-3.xml does not exist and must not: app/sitemaps/[name]/route.ts refuses any name outside the four children with 404 and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, 'so tier-3 cannot exist even as an empty document', and verify-live.ts refuses --wait-sitemap-tier 3 outright ('Tier 3 is noindex and appears in no sitemap child, so waiting for one would never end'). Polling it for this tier's indexable URLs would have waited 20 minutes for a document the design forbids and for URLs that do not exist, because the tier has 0 indexable rows. What was waited for instead was the settling of the three children that do exist.
sitemapCacheWait.settled: Verification ran about 20 minutes after the last batch committed, by which time /sitemaps/pages.xml had rebuilt and the index had settled at 636 dossier URLs.
sitemapCacheWait.whatChangedInTheServedSitemap: pages.xml fell from 4451 URLs (4441 of them legacy-only dossiers) to 10, all of them static pages and none a dossier; browse.xml grew from 1023 to 1843 facet URLs; tier-1.xml and tier-2.xml were untouched at 610 and 26.
sitemapCacheWait.notADefect: Every legacy dossier now has a corpus_pages row, and a Tier 3 row is noindex, so pages.xml correctly stops announcing it. Nothing lost an answer: all 9859 legacy slugs still resolve.

indexNow.why: Tier 3 is noindex and appears in no sitemap child, so it has no URL to announce. Announcing a page to a search engine while telling that engine not to index it would be a contradiction, and R6 forbids it. The corpus-aware script enforces this itself: `npm run discovery:indexnow -- --tier 3 --json` exits with 'Tier 3 records are not indexed and appear in no sitemap, so none is announced', and its --tier flag is bounded to 1 or 2. Tier 1 submitted 610 URLs and Tier 2 submitted 26; the indexable population is unchanged by this load, so nothing new was announced.

issues: The stage opened by closing the blocker the Tier 2 record left for it, which meant changing a loader and one production row before loading anything. scripts/corpus-20k/load/materialise.ts now refuses to write a redirect chain and repairs any it finds; the one broken row was re-pointed and /d/risedronate-sodium-hemipentahydrate answers 308 again. All 870 redirect rows in production answer 308 and the ledger holds no chain. Running Tier 3 without this would have written 176 more redirects into a ledger the route was already failing closed on.

FOR THE SPEC OWNER, NOT A DEFECT. The served sitemap now announces 636 dossier URLs where it announced 5,077 before this load. Nothing was lost - every one of the 9,859 legacy slugs still answers 200, 308 or 410 - but 4,441 dossiers that pages.xml was announcing are now Tier 3 corpus pages carrying noindex, follow. That is the threshold-11 decision and R6 landing together, and it is the first time the whole consequence is visible on the live site. The promotion band is where the population comes back: 2,365 pages hold 7 to 10 present fields, 752 of them in Tier 3.

IndexNow was skipped for this tier, and the tooling refuses it rather than leaving it to judgement: `npm run discovery:indexnow -- --tier 3` exits with 'Tier 3 records are not indexed and appear in no sitemap, so none is announced', and the flag is bounded to 1 or 2. Submitted 0, accepted 0, no ledger entry. Announcing a page to a search engine while telling that engine not to index it would contradict R6.

/sitemaps/tier-3.xml does not exist and returns 404 with X-Robots-Tag: noindex. The instruction to poll it until it lists this tier's indexable URLs cannot be met and should not be: the route refuses the name by design, verify-live.ts refuses --wait-sitemap-tier 3 for the same reason, and the tier has 0 indexable rows. What was waited for instead was the 15-minute settling of the three children that do exist; /sitemaps/pages.xml went from 4,379 URLs mid-load to its settled 10.

4,026 of the 5,350 Tier 3 pages read carry no question block at all. These are name-and-identifier records under R15's stub floor and the template renders what the record holds rather than a heading over nothing, but three quarters of the tier being a stub is the honest shape of what was loaded, and worth stating plainly rather than reporting only that the pages answered 200.

39 of the 145 Tier 3 pages whose suppression classes include S1-S9 carry no supervision block, because they carry no question block at all. Every one of the 39 states its recorded classification in the page header instead ('Regulator classification recorded: S1'), so the safety statement is not lost, but it is not the supervision block the suppression rule describes.

The placeholder scan raised one substring hit across 5,986 fetched pages, on quercetin: 'Telomere Biology Disorders (TBD)', a verbatim ClinicalTrials.gov condition name. It is a source's own abbreviation, not a placeholder. The Tier 2 record has the same finding on an InChIKey, so the substring scan has now raised a false positive twice; a word-boundary scan clears both.

npm run discovery:monitor took 20 minutes 38 seconds over the whole index: 636 record checks plus a 2,033-page walk at the script's 250 ms per-request pace. It completed in one process with no heap failure, so the Tier 1 out-of-memory defect stays closed, but a whole-index run is now a twenty-minute step and the next stage should budget for it.
